blocks.text: How BC poultry farms are bought and sold

parts.t: A working BC poultry farm sells as three things together: the land, the barns and equipment, and the quota. Quota is the right to produce commercially, and a provincial board runs it for each sector:

items.t: : BC Chicken Marketing Board, quota in kilograms of live weight per production period.
: BC Egg Marketing Board, quota counted in laying hens.
: BC Turkey Marketing Board, quota in kilograms of live weight.
Broiler hatching egg farms: BC Broiler Hatching Egg Commission.

parts.t: Quota does not run with the land. Buyer and seller apply to the board together, the barns must be approved premises, and the quota is part of the sale only if the Contract of Purchase and Sale says so. The full explanation:

items.t: Property tax dates depend on where the farm is. A property in a municipality follows that municipality's schedule; a property in a rural area pays provincial rural tax to the Surveyor of Taxes, due July 2, with a 5% penalty on amounts unpaid after July 2 and another 5% on amounts still unpaid after October 31.

faq.a: Check the ALR status, water source and licences, drainage and flood history, the buildings and any quota or production licences that do or do not transfer with the land. Poultry and egg production in BC are supply-managed, so a sale of the farm does not automatically include quota.

faq.a: The Agricultural Land Reserve is farmland protected by the provincial Agricultural Land Commission. Farm use is generally allowed on ALR land, but subdividing, adding homes or using the land for non-farm purposes usually needs approval, so check a property's ALR status before you offer.

faq.q: Who can help me buy or sell in BC?
Does the quota come with a poultry farm when I buy it?
faq.a: Only if the contract says so. Quota does not run with the land: buyer and seller apply to the provincial marketing board for the transfer, and the board approves it and the premises. Write the quota amount and the board-approval condition into the Contract of Purchase and Sale.

faq.q: Can I start a new chicken or egg farm in BC without buying quota?
faq.a: Not at commercial scale. Chicken, egg, turkey and hatching egg production are supply-managed, so producing commercially needs quota issued or transferred with the board's approval. Buying an existing farm with quota is the usual way in.

It matters because the quota, board and production cycle are different assets. A broiler farm sells meat birds grown in eight-week allocation periods set through Chicken Farmers of Canada, while a layer farm's value sits in egg quota under a different board. Confirm which board's quota is actually included in the sale, in writing, before valuing barns or land.
faq.q: Is a chicken farm a broiler farm or an egg farm — and why does it matter at purchase?

faq.a: Not on the quota you bought. The Province's own disease order lists the BC Chicken Marketing Board and the BC Egg Marketing Board as separate regulators with separate quota holders, and each sector's transfer rules live with its own board.
